priceSnapshot.note: The morning add is working and the market has turned over completely underneath it. Morning published at 85,985.0; four hours and twenty-one minutes later spot is 86,621.5, up 636.5 points or 0.74 percent on the handover and up 0.89 percent on the 24-hour open of 85,855.6. The session low was 85,455.0, which is 129.8 points ABOVE the 85,325.2 reduce gate - the gate was never tested this session, unlike overnight. The session high is 86,731.0. The single most important fact in this file is not the price but what produced it: the liquidation tape has FLIPPED SIDES. Morning measured an 11.5-to-1 LONG flush; the last hour and forty-eight minutes ran 1,036,925 USD of SHORT liquidations against 86,493 USD of longs, a 12.0-to-1 SHORT squeeze, and 749,535 USD of it discharged in a single 86,750.0 bucket. The 17:00 UTC hour is in progress at 86,622.1 and has already poked 86,634.2, which is 1.6 points through the morning's 86,632.6 continuation gate - but the bar has not settled, so by this desk's own standing rule the gate has NOT fired.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below 85,325.2, unchanged for the third consecutive report. It survived the overnight test by 19.7 points on a settled-close basis and was never approached this session - the 85,455.0 session low stopped 129.8 points above it. There is no reason to move a level the market has not argued with.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above 86,632.6 - the same continuation gate morning wrote, deliberately unchanged even though the in-progress 17:00 UTC bar has already traded 86,634.2 through it. A wick is not a close. That rule is 3-for-3 this week and it is the reason the 85,325.2 gate held overnight instead of stopping the book out at the 85,111.1 spike low. When it settles above, the next tranche goes to work with only 86,899.8 and the 87,399.0 eight-month high overhead.

decisionBox.changed: Position stays ADD for a second consecutive session, and the size is where the discipline lives rather than the direction. This session deploys 12.0 USDT of spot - a deliberately small tranche against morning's larger one - and the reason is a rule this desk wrote down itself. The endday lesson from 21 September says to grade a decision by the CLASS of evidence behind it: a momentum oscillator at an extreme is a SIZING input and never a trigger, while a pre-committed price level or a measurable positioning series is a valid trigger. Applied literally here, the 4H RSI at 76.56 - the hottest reading of the day, up from 75.18 at morning - argues for a SMALLER add, not for selling. Selling a working long on an oscillator print alone is precisely the 21 September morning error that trimmed at 84,742.7 and is still the standing entry in this book's error log. Three measurable structural facts carry the trigger side. FIRST, positioning has inverted in the wallet's favour: the OKX long/short account ratio has walked 0.99, 0.96, 0.95, 0.94 across the last four hourly buckets, so accounts are now NET SHORT into a breakout, and that is fuel rather than overhang. SECOND, funding settled at 0.0000217, effectively the floor - nobody is paying to hold these longs, so the rally is not leverage-financed. THIRD, open interest is 2,642,096,203 USD, up 0.71 percent from morning while price rose 0.74 percent, which is orderly participation rather than a blow-off. Against that, the 86,750.0 short-liquidation magnet directly overhead has ALREADY discharged 749,535 USD, so the easiest fuel above has been spent - which is the second reason the tranche is small. The reduce gate, the invalidation and the resting stop are all unchanged.

liquidation.note: 749,535 USD of SHORT liquidations against zero longs across 22 fills - by far the largest cluster in the window and 128.5 points above spot. This is where the squeeze actually killed leverage. Realized fills map where leverage has already died, not where stops rest now, and here that cuts against the bulls: the short fuel at this shelf has been spent, so a push through it has less mechanical help than the raw size suggests.
261,835 USD of short liquidations across 55 fills, the most numerous bucket in the window. Now 121.5 points below spot and acting as the floor the squeeze built on the way up.

47,112 USD split near-evenly, 21,607 long against 25,505 short across 8 fills. A genuine two-way pocket and the only balanced bucket on the tape - it marks the pivot where the session flipped from long flush to short squeeze.

64,886 USD of LONG liquidations against 52 USD of shorts across 15 fills, 621.5 points below spot. The last place longs were hurt before the reversal, which makes it the first real shelf on a pullback.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is up, but for a positioning reason rather than a liquidation-size reason, and the distinction matters. The raw tape shows 1,036,925 USD of shorts against 86,493 USD of longs liquidated, a 12.0-to-1 squeeze - the exact mirror of morning's 11.5-to-1 long flush. Almost all of it, 749,535 USD, discharged INTO the 86,750.0 bucket, so that magnet has largely been paid out and is weaker than its size implies. What keeps the pull up is the account ratio: 0.99, 0.96, 0.95, 0.94 over the last four hourly buckets, a steady walk into net-short positioning while price rose. Accounts are leaning against this move, funding is at the floor at 0.0000217 so they are being paid almost nothing to do it, and open interest is up 0.71 percent. That is unfinished business above, and it is why the nearestAbove is named even though its fuel is partly spent.

calibration.note: Morning was right on both halves and the row records both. The READ: the reduce gate at 85,325.2 was never threatened - the 85,455.0 session low stopped 129.8 points above it, so priorReduceFired is false for the second consecutive session. The continuation add gate at 86,632.6 has NOT fired either, and this is the interesting part: the in-progress 17:00 UTC hour traded 86,634.2, which is 1.6 points THROUGH the level, and the desk is still calling it unfired because the bar has not settled. That is the same wick-is-not-a-close rule that saved the book overnight when price spiked 214.1 points below the reduce gate and the lowest settled close missed it by 19.7 points. Holding the rule when it costs you an entry is what makes it worth having when it saves you an exit. The TRADE: morning added spot at 85,985.0 and the mark is 86,621.5, so that tranche is 636.5 points or 0.74 percent onside and actingHelped is true. The standing error remains the 21 September morning trim at 84,742.7, now 1,878.8 points offside - it keeps getting more expensive, and naming it is the point. This session's small size is the direct application of the lesson that produced that error: the 4H RSI at 76.56 sizes the tranche down, it does not sell the position.
